newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says gets $5 bln credits since U.S. embargo.
newsitem.headline: Iran says gets $5 bln credits since U.S. embargo.

text.p: Iran has received foreign credits worth $5 billion since shortly after the United States imposed sanctions on the Islamic republic in 1995, Iranian Central Bank Governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh said on Monday.
Iran had received the $5 billion to use in large development projects since September 1995 "despite the plots by America", said Nourbakhsh, quoted by the daily Kayhan newspaper.
He was referring to the trade and investment ban imposed in June 1995 by Washington against Tehran.

"The conspiracies by America in this area have been fruitless, as Italy, Germany, Britain, the Scandinavian countries and France have announced they would cooperate with the Islamic Republic of Iran," Nourbakhsh said. He did not elaborate.
Nourbakhsh said Iran's foreign debt stood at $19.55 billion at the end of 1996, of which $10 billion were rescheduled debts, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
Iran's total foreign commitments would reach $25 billion by the end of the country's second development plan in March 2000, he said.
Tehran would repay $3.7 billion of its debt in 1997, $3.3 billion in 1998, $1.9 billion in 1999, and $182 million in the year 2000, Nourbakhsh was quoted by the agency as saying.
